rulings.title: §9 item 2's re-run criterion ("each of the 38 gains its simps") is false for six of the 38 (class `fixes` parameters, short-circuited by ①)
rulings.reason: CONFIRMED at source, independently of both verifiers, and it is the one finding of this round with a concrete consequence. (1) The rule: `own_defining_axioms` is `if is_some (class_param_of env const_name) then [] else …` (Tools/semantic_digest.ML:387-388), with `class_param_of = Axclass.class_of_param` (:339-340), which reads the Axclass params table filled by `map_params (fold (fn (x,_) => add_param ctxt (x, class)) params)` (Pure/axclass.ML:433) — i.e. exactly the class `fixes` parameters — and answers through `AList.lookup (op =) (params_of thy)` (axclass.ML:144). So for a class `fixes` parameter ② is never computed and ③ can never fire, whatever the registry holds. (2) Six of CENSUS's 38 are such parameters, verified in the distribution, not inferred: `class exhaustive = term_of + fixes exhaustive` and `class full_exhaustive = term_of + fixes full_exhaustive` (HOL/Quickcheck_Exhaustive.thy:19-25); `class semiring_bit_operations = semiring_bits + fixes "and" … and or … and xor` (HOL/Bit_Operations.thy:612-615); `class small_lazy = fixes small_lazy` (HOL/Lazy_Sequence.thy:214-215). All six are in CENSUS.md's table of the 38 (CENSUS.md:377, :379, :380). (3) The seventh `_class.` name among the 38, `…bit_operations_class.or_num`, is correctly excluded: CENSUS.md:157-159 measures `own_defining_axioms` = 1 for it (`…_class.or_num_dict`), which is possible only with `class_param_of` = NONE, and CENSUS.md:415-416 keeps it inside the 19 reached. (4) The plan misquotes CENSUS against CENSUS's own definition: CENSUS.md:337-339 defines "reached by the new branch" as the self-keyed query result AND not short-circuited by ①, and its shape table applies that clause at :351; PLAN.md:377-378 drops the second half and demands "each of the 38 gains its simps". (5) It also contradicts a measurement already in the plan's own verification record: VERIFICATION.md:340-342, "34 of 40 change, 6 do not. The 6 that do not are exactly the 6 class parameters, protected by `class_param_of`" — and the two constants that separate the Spec_Rules 40 from the registry 38 (`fold2_bit_int.F`, the locale twin, CENSUS.md:394-399) are neither of them class parameters, so 38 − 6 = 32 is exact, not a sample. (6) It contradicts the plan four bullets earlier (PLAN.md:99-101) and a live assertion of the suite under review (Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy:57-60, S2d/S2e pin `null (own_defining_axioms env "Groups.plus_class.plus")`), which PLAN.md:291 keeps. This is residue of round-two ruling def-1, whose fix ordered §9 item 2's expected values rewritten from the pre-flight census; the rewrite took CENSUS's raw 38 instead of CENSUS's criterion. It is squarely round-three question (2) and (3), not a re-opened decision, and round two's own precedent applies verbatim (normaliser-1: "Writing a known-false criterion into an acceptance is worse than the containment criterion the plan has"). Both rebuttals' reduction to minor is accepted — no code, no decision and no other figure moves (the 19-of-20 at PLAN.md:117-118 is untouched; none of the six is in CENSUS.md:411-420) — but the edit at :377-378 is mandatory, because a CORRECT implementation goes red on it and the implementer would either patch working code or burn a round.
rulings.fix: MANDATORY, one hand edit (no scripted edits — PLAN.md is a plan document). PLAN.md:377-378: replace "check that each of the 38 gains its simps and that `fold2_bit_int.F` does not" with the partition, reporting both `class_param_of` and `own_defining_axioms` in the same one REPL evaluation: the 32 non-parameters each gain their simps; the six class `fixes` parameters (`Quickcheck_Exhaustive.exhaustive_class.exhaustive`, `…full_exhaustive_class.full_exhaustive`, `Lazy_Sequence.small_lazy_class.small_lazy`, `Bit_Operations.semiring_bit_operations_class.{and,or,xor}`) keep `own_defining_axioms = []` by rule ① (semantic_digest.ML:387-388), as S2d/S2e already assert for `Groups.plus_class.plus`; and `fold2_bit_int.F` gains nothing. RECOMMENDED, one clause: PLAN.md:114, after "38 constants are self-keyed in the registry", insert "(six of them class `fixes` parameters that ① short-circuits, so ③ moves 32 digests)" — copy CENSUS.md:337-339's own criterion for the wording. Do not restate the bullet: its conclusion at PLAN.md:118-119 ("All sit in loaded, persistent theories and pay nothing") is true at either number. Nothing else changes — not the rule, not §4, not the 19-of-20.

rulings.title: Same defect as A-1, found independently: §2 and §9 item 2 read CENSUS's 38 as the set ③ moves; the number is 32 and §9 item 2 fails on a correct implementation

The 6 that do not are exactly the 6 class parameters") as a measurement ALREADY IN THE RECORD that PLAN.md:377-378 contradicts, and it locates the harm precisely — consequence (i), the cost sentence at PLAN.md:112-117, is inert because all 38 sit in persistent theories that never compute a digest (PLAN.md:109-112, semantic_store.ML:1795-1808), while consequence (ii), the acceptance at PLAN.md:377-378, is the whole of the defect. Its carve-out of `…_class.or_num` is correct (CENSUS.md:157-159, :415-416), so PLAN.md:116-118's "19 of 20" stands. Ruled together with A-1: one edit closes both.
rulings.fix: See A-1. One mandatory edit at PLAN.md:377-378, one recommended clause at PLAN.md:114. B-1's proposed replacement text and A-1's are equivalent; either may be used verbatim.

rulings.title: §2's locale-target sentence asserts a mechanism ("keyed on the registration morphism's image") that the CENSUS measurement it cites refutes
rulings.reason: The headline claim is false and the residue is below the bar. PLAN.md:77-82 is a RESTRICTIVE statement — a locale-target `fun` reaches the background theory "only through that locale's registrations, keyed on the registration morphism's image, never on the bare constant". CENSUS (b) measures zero keys of any kind for `fold2_bit_int.F` and for the three `global_interpretation … defines` images (CENSUS.md:107, :124-127, :139-141). Zero is silence about a channel, not a counterexample to a restriction; it cannot "refute" the clause, and the finding concedes the parenthetical quotes CENSUS accurately. Nor is the mechanism unmeasured: the very next sentence (PLAN.md:83-85) cites CENSUS (c), where the class operation `…_class.or_num` carries 1 entry with 9 simps while its locale-level twin carries 0 (CENSUS.md:155-184) — a class IS a locale and its class operation is the registration morphism's image, and I confirmed the class target routes through `Generic_Target.locale_declaration` exactly as the locale target does (Pure/Isar/named_target.ML:108 and :116 both bind `declaration = Generic_Target.locale_declaration …`; generic_target.ML:464-468 is `pervasive ? background_declaration #> locale_target_declaration #> standard_declaration`), so with `pervasive = false` (function.ML:135-136, :215-216) that theory-level key cannot have come from `background_declaration`. §2 and §7 are not "the same case two ways": §7 (PLAN.md:308-311) is the narrower `global_interpretation` statement. What is left after the headline falls is a preference for deleting four words from a clause with no consequence — ③ does not fire either way, no number, test, criterion or decision moves, as the finding itself concedes. That is the style-only / "reword this" class SCOPE.md:93-97 orders rejected harshly. Rejected as refuted.
rulings.fix: None required. If the user wants the free tidy-up anyway it is a four-word deletion at PLAN.md:79-80 (", keyed on the registration morphism's image"), since the positive instance is already carried by the next sentence — but do NOT treat it as a condition of 开工.

rulings.title: §5 option (a) still names "§9 item 3 (ii)" as change 2's discriminator, but merge-3 rewrote (ii) into a seed COUNT that `narquil` alone satisfies
rulings.reason: Verified end to end, including the arithmetic, which is measured rather than hypothetical. The clause is at PLAN.md:237-238: option (a) would "state that change 2 keeps no standing in-suite guard — its discriminator is §9 item 3 (ii)". It was written to round-two ruling normaliser-1's fix text, which named "§9 item 3 (ii)'s requirement that `galmuth` appear in the seed set". Round-two ruling merge-3 then destroyed that version of (ii) ("the dry run reports a seed COUNT, never the seed set"), and rev 2.2 applied merge-3 at PLAN.md:386-392: "the go/no-go is that N exceeds the 26 recorded for the same A1→B transition in acceptance_step10 run 2 (… the count does not attribute)". The 26 is real (ai-artifacts/acceptance_step10/REPORT.md:42, run 2, "1 theory, N = 26"). And change 1 ALONE clears it: VERIFICATION.md's Gal_Probe table measures `narquil`'s digest under direction A as `296e82bb…` (A) vs `6e78fdee…` (B) → CHANGED, with the normaliser still in place, while `galmuth`'s is identical in both, and acceptance_step10/REPORT.md:88 records galmuth as "not a seed" today. So N ≥ 27 > 26 with a surviving normaliser, and (ii) discriminates change 1, never change 2. Attribution did survive, but only as "OBSERVATION, not a criterion" (PLAN.md:402-405), which is not a discriminator either. Both the finder and the rebuttal scoped it correctly: §8 records option (b) chosen (PLAN.md:360-363), so nothing in the shipped path breaks — but SCOPE.md:166-167 puts "a cross-reference that resolves to nothing" in this round's remit by name, and the sentence is not inert: the (a)/(b) choice turned on whether change 2 has a discriminator, so a reader reopening (a) is told it is better covered than it is. Minor, editorial, fix.
rulings.fix: One hand edit at PLAN.md:237-238, and the smallest honest form is a deletion: strike "— its discriminator is §9 item 3 (ii)", leaving "…and state that change 2 keeps no standing in-suite guard;". If option (a) should keep telling a future reader what evidence would then remain, the finder's replacement is accurate and may be used verbatim: "…keeps no standing in-suite guard — the only two-sided evidence for change 2 would then be §9 item 3 (iii)'s OBSERVATION that a `gate:`/`verdict:` line names `constant Sim_Measure_A1.galmuth`, since (ii)'s N > 26 is cleared by `narquil` alone." §8 and §9 are already correct and do not change.

rulings.title: §9 item 1's "the new assertions FAIL on the current code" cannot be executed for the chosen §5 (b) guard: `digest_term` is not exported today
rulings.reason: Verified. §8 chose option (b): `digest_term` is exported and the single assertion `digest_term t = Term_Digest.term128 t` is change 2's standing guard (PLAN.md:238-244, :360-363). Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy:5 loads the module by source (`ML_file ‹…/Tools/semantic_digest.ML›`), so the suite sees today's signature verbatim: SEMANTIC_DIGEST runs from semantic_digest.ML:31 to :66 and exports `normalize` (:48), `semantics_of` (:61) and `own_defining_axioms` (:65) — `digest_term` is defined unexported at :178. An `ML ‹…›` block naming `Semantic_Digest.digest_term` therefore raises an unbound-identifier error against unmodified code; it never reaches `check` and never prints FAIL, so PLAN.md:369-371's "the new assertions FAIL on the current code and PASS after" is not satisfiable for this one assertion. The finding's own recipe is correct and is what makes this a one-clause repair rather than a design problem: with only the `val digest_term` signature line added and `normalize` still in the pipeline the assertion is genuinely red (`norm_typ` renames a TFree at :144-146 and `norm_term` a Free at :153-157; the file's own comment at :117-121 records that `Term_Digest.term128` hashes TFree/Free names), and green after change 2. I accept the rebuttal's trims to the title — the module loads, and an unbound-identifier error is an unambiguous not-green signal — but not its conclusion that nothing survives: round-three question (4) asks precisely whether the §5 (b) guard FAILS today and PASSES after, and as written the acceptance step for it cannot be run. One clause of prose, minor.
rulings.fix: Fold into the single rewrite of PLAN.md:369-371 shared with B-5 (see B-5's fix). The clause this finding contributes: the change-2 guard is the exception to "FAIL today" — it names `digest_term`, which today's signature does not export, so on unmodified code it errors instead of printing FAIL; to see it red first, add only the `val digest_term` signature line and run it while `normalize` is still in the pipeline.

rulings.title: §6 says hoisting the new test subjects would "change the input of seven live assertions"; the file-level env is the input of far more than seven
rulings.reason: Confirmed by my own enumeration of Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy, and no reading yields seven. The file-level `env` is built at :20 and reaches the checks directly or through the helpers `deps_of`/`mentions`/`mentions_kind` (:27-31). Checks that consume it: S1a/S1b (:37, :39), S2a-S2e (:47, :49, :54, :57, :59), S3a/S3b (:80, :85 — these use `deps_of`, i.e. the file env, not the local `env2` of :75), S4a/S4b (:132, :136), S5a/S5b (:143, :145), S6/S6b (:152, :159), S7 (:178, one `check` call executed twice by `map cmp ["Rings.idom", "Rings.comm_ring_1"]` at :179), S10/S10b/S10c (:237, :239, :242), S11b/S11c (:280, :285), S12 (:313) — 22 `check` call sites, 23 executions. Seven is the count of the constant-level block S1a-S2e alone; by coincidence the complement (S3c, S3d, S3e, S8a, S8b, S9, S11a) is also exactly seven, so neither candidate origin names the set the sentence claims. The input really would change: `env` is `{thy, axioms, locale_parents}` with `axioms = Symtab.make_distinct (Theory.all_axioms_of thy)` (semantic_digest.ML:75-82, :98-100), and declaring a `fun` above :20 adds its `Defs` axiom and moves `thy`. `grep -n seven PLAN.md` returns only :273, so there is no other section to reconcile against. The design decision the sentence defends is right and unaffected — an implementer does the same thing either way — but this is a checkable factual error in the object under review, which is round-three question (3), not a style remark. I adopt the rebuttal's tightening: prefer the count-free wording, because hoisting also perturbs the checks at :75, :109, :192, :218 and :270, so any number written there can go stale again.
rulings.fix: Hand-edit PLAN.md:273-274: replace "(that would change the input of seven live assertions)" with "(that would change the input of every assertion built on the file-level env)". If a number is insisted on it is 22 call sites / 23 executions, not seven — but the count-free form is the one to ship.

rulings.title: The §5 (b) guard's witness term contains only a `Free` and a `TFree`, so two of the deleted `norm_term`'s four clauses can be reintroduced with the guard still green, while :243 claims it goes red under ANY pre-hash transform
rulings.reason: The scope claim is true and I could not break it. The deleted transform has four independent name/index-touching clauses, each separately visible to the hasher: `norm_typ` on TFree (semantic_digest.ML:144-146) and TVar (:147-149), `norm_term` on Free (:153-157), on Var (:158-162, which also zeroes the index) and on Abs (:164-169, binder name replaced by ""), with Bound/Const/application pass-through (:151-152, :163, :170-174); and the hasher's own comment records that `Term_Digest.term128` hashes Abs binder names and TFree/TVar names (:117-121). A `t` containing only a `Free` and a `TFree` is therefore blind to a transform touching only Abs binder names or only Vars, so PLAN.md:242-243's "which goes red under ANY pre-hash transform" is false as written, in the sentence that is simultaneously the decision record and the implementation instruction for the ONLY standing in-suite guard change 2 has (PLAN.md:236-238 records that option (a)'s alternative was to have none). Round-three question (4) is answered in the plan's favour — the assertion does FAIL today and PASS after (A-4's signature caveat aside) and is not satisfiable through an unrelated path, since it names `Semantic_Digest.digest_term` and `Term_Digest.term128` directly, unlike the S3e/S8 shapes it replaces, whose only production reference was `Semantic_Digest.normalize` at Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy:122 and :194. But CLAUDE.md's elegance rule is explicit that a shape making the invariant impossible to violate beats one asking people to remember it, and enriching the witness term costs one term literal. I accept the rebuttal's two corrections: the regression the guard actually exists for — wholesale restoration of `fun digest_term t = Term_Digest.term128 (normalize t)` — IS caught by the minimal term, so this is a coverage widening rather than a hole; and the finding's offer to "keep ANY, now earned" must be refused, since even the enriched term is blind to a Bound-index or sort-stripping transform. The mandatory half is the word, not the term.
rulings.fix: One hand edit at PLAN.md:242-243. Mandatory: replace "which goes red under ANY pre-hash transform" with "which goes red under any of the transforms `normalize` performed" — the word ANY is not earned by either term. Recommended in the same edit (zero implementation cost, and the implementer's under F7 either way): specify `t` as containing a `Free`, a `TFree`, a schematic `Var` with a non-zero index and an `Abs` with a non-empty binder name, e.g. `Abs ("y", TFree ("'a", []), Free ("x", TFree ("'b", [])) $ Bound 0 $ Var (("v", 3), TFree ("'c", [])))`, so that each clause of the deleted `norm_term` (semantic_digest.ML:144-149, :153-157, :158-162, :164-169) is red on its own. The assertion stays one line and the signature still grows by one entry.

rulings.title: rev 2.2 cites review-ruling ids from two rounds without saying which round, the two namespaces collide on `elegance-2`/`elegance-4`, and neither round's rulings are in the repository
rulings.reason: Verified, including the rebuttal's corrections, which I confirmed and adopt. `grep` over PLAN.md gives EIGHT anchors, not the finding's seven: `elegance-4` :171, `def2-4` :190, `def-5` :194, `elegance-2` :234, `normaliser-1` :248, `merge-2` :278, `def1-2` :301, `def2-2` :350 — so four of the finding's line numbers are off by one to three and it omits `def2-2` at :350. The collision is real: round one's namespace is `def1-*`/`def2-*`/`elegance-1..4` and round two's is `merge-*`/`normaliser-*`/`elegance-1..6`/`def-*`, and I read both journals — round one's `elegance-4` is "`Proof_Context.init_global` per constant contradicts the file's per-pass env discipline" (which is what PLAN.md:170-171 means) while round two's is the prop-list-order finding; round one's `elegance-2` is "the branch's theory safety rests on an unstated caller invariant" while round two's is the S3e/S8 guard finding (which is what PLAN.md:234 means). Nothing in the plan says which round any id belongs to, though PLAN.md:318 does name rounds in prose ("rejected twice (review rounds 1 and 2)"), so the plan is inconsistent with itself about its own citation style. And the record is absent: `ls ai-artifacts/fun_digest/review/` returns SCOPE.md and nothing else, while PLAN.md:3-5 offers that directory as the record of "two adversarial review rounds". The decisive point is the repository's own convention, which I checked: the sibling `ai-artifacts/review_integration/` holds `judge.json`, `rereview_judge.json` and `rereview2_judge.json` beside its SCOPE.md. So the house pattern for archiving rulings exists and this directory does not follow it. In scope by SCOPE.md:166-167 ("a cross-reference that resolves to nothing") and by round two's own def-3, which ruled the identical class "fix". I adopt the rebuttal's refutation of the two aggravating clauses — each id sits in a sentence stating its subject, so a journal-holding reader resolves it uniquely, and three round-one anchors are traceable in-repo through SCOPE.md:125-129 — and its severity: zero implementation impact, since every anchor's substance is restated inline. Minor, fix.
rulings.fix: Two hand edits plus two file drops — not eight edits. (1) Qualify only the two colliding ids, since the other six are unique across both namespaces: PLAN.md:171 "— elegance-4" → "— round-one elegance-4"; PLAN.md:234 "(elegance-2)" → "(round-two elegance-2)". (2) Make PLAN.md:3-5's pointer true by following the existing house pattern in ai-artifacts/review_integration/: extract each round's judge ruling verbatim from its workflow journal (the last {"type":"result"} object containing "readiness" in ~/.claude/projects/-home-qiyuan-Current-MLML/8ee4dc8b-0295-46df-b280-a85bcc774433/subagents/workflows/wf_e3220232-065/journal.jsonl and .../wf_48c37aa2-473/journal.jsonl) into ai-artifacts/fun_digest/review/judge.json and .../rereview_judge.json. That resolves all eight anchors at once and costs no prose. If the user prefers not to archive them, reword PLAN.md:3-5 so `review/` is offered as the rounds' scope rather than their record, and keep edit (1). Either way include the eighth site (def2-2 at :350) in whatever pass is made — this round's fix for it is "leave it, it is unique", but do not let a later sweep miss it.

rulings.title: Adding `ctxt` to the `env` record falsifies the signature comment at semantic_digest.ML:33-34, and §4's comment list does not schedule it for repair
rulings.reason: Rejected, and named: this is the "consider adding a comment" class that SCOPE.md:96 orders rejected harshly, and round two already rejected it once in the same file — normaliser-4's sub-item (f) was thrown out with "splitting its banner from its commentary is the 'consider adding a comment' class". The facts are right as far as they go: semantic_digest.ML:33-34 reads "Per-pass precomputed state: the indexed axiom table and the locale-parent index. Building these per entity would be quadratic." over the record at :75-82, PLAN.md:168-171 adds `ctxt = Proof_Context.init_global thy` to it, and PLAN.md:207-216 lists three comment sites without :33-34. But three things sink it as a defect of rev 2.2. First, "falsifies" overstates: `thy` (:76) has always been in the record and never in that enumeration, so the comment was never a field-by-field contract, and PLAN.md:171 itself says `ctxt` is there for env discipline and not for cost — it belongs in `thy`'s category, not as a third index. Second, it was never a round-two ruling: the round-two result carries fifteen rulings (merge-1..4, normaliser-1/3/4, elegance-2/5/6, def-1..5) and none concerns :33-34; the sentence quoted is an aside inside `proposals_for_user`, so round-three question (1) does not reach it. Third, the miss-risk is absent — the implementer must edit that same signature block three times (delete `val normalize` with its comment at :46-48, add `val digest_term`, restate :63-65 per PLAN.md:212), thirteen lines below :33-34 — and F7 (PLAN.md:148) puts comments in the implementer's hands by decision. The distinction from the round-two sites that DID survive is exactly the one normaliser-4 drew: those were in other documents the implementer would never open. Rejected as a nitpick.
rulings.fix: None. If the user nonetheless wants it written down, it is one clause appended to PLAN.md:212 — "and the env comment at `:33-34`, which must also name the global proof context, held for the registry query (`retrieve_function_data` takes a `Proof.context`, function_common.ML:277-281), not because building it per entity would be quadratic" — but do not make it a condition of 开工, and keep the code comment itself short, per the project's comment rule.

rulings.title: §9 item 1 says every new assertion fails today, which is false of the three controls §6 mandates
rulings.reason: Confirmed at the sources rather than from the plan's say-so. PLAN.md:369-371 reads "the new assertions FAIL on the current code and PASS after; all other assertions unchanged (S3e/S8 deleted per §5)" — and "all other assertions" covers the suite's pre-existing checks, not §6's new ones, so the three controls at PLAN.md:287-289 (a `primrec`, a `definition`, a `partial_function (option)` keeping exactly their `Defs` axiom) fall under the universal claim and contradict it. They pass both before and after: today's `own_defining_axioms` returns the `same_theory`-filtered `Defs` axioms whenever that list is non-empty and only falls through to `spec_rule_axioms` when it is empty (semantic_digest.ML:387-399), and all three shapes carry a body-carrying `Defs` axiom, one entry each (VERIFICATION.md:110 `hovrik ≡ option.fixp_fun (…)`, :112 `pr_len ≡ rec_list 0 (λx xs. Suc)`, :114 `mulgrav_def_raw`, each marked "body in Defs? YES"); declared in the test theory itself, `same_theory` holds. After ③ they are unchanged, because the registry has exactly two writers, both in `function.ML` (PLAN.md:54-58), so `retrieve_function_data` has no entry for any of the three. A control that went red today would mean the suite was broken. Not a re-opened decision: round two touched §9 item 1 only through def-4 (the Test_All cost claim), which rev 2.2 applied at PLAN.md:371-374. I accept the rebuttal's demolition of the finding's stated harm — §6 annotates each discriminating check individually (PLAN.md:277, :281-283, :285-286) and pointedly does not annotate the controls, so no implementer is misled — but not its conclusion: the realistic cost is at §9 item 4's post-implementation review, where a reviewer checking the shipped suite against item 1 as written could flag three green controls as non-discriminating and press to delete them, losing the F3 pin against a `Spec_Rules` source (PLAN.md:289). One clause of prose, minor.
rulings.fix: One hand edit at PLAN.md:369-371, combining this with A-4. Replace "the new assertions FAIL on the current code and PASS after; all other assertions unchanged (S3e/S8 deleted per §5)" with: "every new assertion §6 annotates as discriminating FAILS on the current code and PASSES after; §6's three controls, like S2d/S2e, pass both before and after; the change-2 guard is the one exception to 'FAILS today' — it names `digest_term`, which today's signature does not export (semantic_digest.ML:31-66), so on unmodified code it errors rather than printing FAIL; to see it red first, add only the `val digest_term` signature line and run it while `normalize` is still in the pipeline. All other assertions unchanged (S3e/S8 deleted per §5)." Do NOT enumerate the discriminating assertions inside §9 — §6 stays the single list, so the two sections cannot drift apart again.

summary:
READY_AFTER_FIXES. Rev 2.2 is sound where it matters: I re-checked every round-two "fix" ruling against the plan and the code and all thirteen are present and true — merge-1's key filter and the two-branch net statement (PLAN.md:65-82, :174-179), merge-2's MERGE pin (:278-283), merge-3's count-based go/no-go (:386-392), merge-4's narquil-CHANGED criterion with the fail-safe argument and galmuth demoted to an observation (:393-408), normaliser-1's correction of the Test_All determinism block (:245-248), normaliser-3's re-interpretation cost and no-baseline exception (:40-44, :258-265), normaliser-4's 四条→三条, both §14 cells and semantics.py:318 (:249-257) plus the extended NOTE (:10-16), elegance-2 settled by §8 option (b) (:230-248, :360-363), def-1's pre-flight census now taken on the registry (CENSUS.md) with §2/§7/§9 rewritten from it, def-2's two-writers justification in the F2 row (:143), def-3's three dangling pointers all repointed (no "§7 item 2" remains; the "(§8)" is gone at :126-128), def-4's restated Test_All claim (:371-374), and def-5's sort-together clause (:192-196). Round-three question (4) is answered in the plan's favour: the §6 MERGE pin and the §5 (b) guard each discriminate, and neither is satisfiable through an unrelated path — the guard names `Semantic_Digest.digest_term` and `Term_Digest.term128` directly, unlike the S3e/S8 shapes it replaces, whose only production reference was `Semantic_Digest.normalize` at Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy:122 and :194.

Nine findings, seven upheld, two rejected. Rejected by name: A-2 (reject-refuted — CENSUS (b)'s zero keys cannot refute a restrictive "only through registrations, never on the bare constant", and the mechanism has a measured positive instance two lines later in CENSUS (c); what is left is a four-word rewording with no consequence) and B-4 (reject-nitpick — the "consider adding a comment" class SCOPE.md:96 orders rejected and round two already rejected once as normaliser-4(f); it was never a round-two ruling, and F7 puts comments with the implementer, who must edit that very signature block).

One finding blocks 开工, and both verifiers found it independently: A-1 = B-1. PLAN.md:377-378 tells the implementer to run `own_defining_axioms` over CENSUS's 38 self-keyed constants and expect "each of the 38 gains its simps". Six of the 38 are class `fixes` parameters — `exhaustive_class.exhaustive`, `full_exhaustive_class.full_exhaustive`, `semiring_bit_operations_class.{and,or,xor}`, `small_lazy_class.small_lazy`, verified as `fixes` in Quickcheck_Exhaustive.thy:19-25, Bit_Operations.thy:612-615 and Lazy_Sequence.thy:214-215 — and rule ① returns [] for them before any axiom source is consulted (semantic_digest.ML:387-388 through Axclass.class_of_param, axclass.ML:144/:433). So ③ reaches 32, not 38, and a CORRECT implementation goes red on that acceptance. The plan contradicts CENSUS's own criterion (CENSUS.md:337-339, applied at :351), its own §2 four bullets earlier (PLAN.md:99-101), a measurement already in its verification record (VERIFICATION.md:340-342, "the 6 that do not are exactly the 6 class parameters"), and a live assertion of the suite it keeps (Test_Sensitivity.thy:57-60). This is residue of round-two ruling def-1, and round two's own normaliser-1 settled the principle: writing a known-false criterion into an acceptance is worse than a weaker true one. The 19-of-20 figure is untouched; `…_class.or_num` is correctly excluded as a class definition, not a parameter (CENSUS.md:157-159).

The other six upheld findings are prose defects with no design consequence, each one hand edit: A-3 (a stale cross-reference in the UNchosen §5 option (a) — merge-3's rewrite left "its discriminator is §9 item 3 (ii)" pointing at a seed COUNT that `narquil` alone clears, VERIFICATION.md's Gal_Probe table vs acceptance_step10/REPORT.md:42), A-4 and B-5 (two separate errors in the one sentence PLAN.md:369-371 — the change-2 guard cannot print FAIL today because `digest_term` is unexported, and §6's three controls must pass both before and after; one combined rewrite closes both), A-5 ("seven live assertions" at PLAN.md:273 — the file-level env feeds 22 check sites / 23 executions; ship the count-free wording), B-2 ("goes red under ANY pre-hash transform" at PLAN.md:243 is false — the minimal witness term is blind to the deleted `norm_term`'s Abs and Var clauses; drop "ANY", and enriching the term costs one literal), and B-3 (eight ruling-id anchors from two colliding namespaces, none archived in `review/`; qualify the two homonyms and drop the two judge rulings into `review/` as the sibling `ai-artifacts/review_integration/` already does).

Condition to start: seven hand edits to PLAN.md — no scripted edits, it is a plan document — of which only PLAN.md:377-378 is load-bearing; optionally the two ruling files into `review/`. Nothing touches the rule, the merge, the census, F1–F7 or §8, and no measurement needs re-taking. Once those are in, 开工.
